verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 48.53
verses.english: Linked Discourses 48.53

verses.pali: 6. Sūkarakhatavagga
verses.english: 6. The Boar’s Cave

verses.pali: Sekhasutta
verses.english: A Trainee

verses.pali: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
verses.english: So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī, in Ghosita’s Monastery.

verses.pali: Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: “atthi nu kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajāneyya, asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajāneyyā”ti?
verses.english: “Mendicants, is there a way that a mendicant who is a trainee, standing at the level of a trainee, can understand that they are a trainee? And that a mendicant who is an adept, standing at the level of an adept, can understand that they are an adept?”

verses.pali: “Bhagavaṁmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā …pe…
verses.english: “Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

verses.pali: “atthi, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajāneyya, asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajāneyya.
verses.english: “There is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee, standing at the level of a trainee, can understand that they are a trainee, and that a mendicant who is an adept, standing at the level of an adept, can understand that they are an adept.

verses.pali: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajānāti?
verses.english: And what is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee can understand that they are a trainee?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti—
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant who is a trainee truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

verses.pali: ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: This is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee can understand that they are a trainee.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati:
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant who is a trainee reflects:

verses.pali: ‘atthi nu kho ito bahiddhā añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo evaṁ bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ tathaṁ dhammaṁ deseti yathā bhagavā’ti?
verses.english: ‘Is there any other ascetic or brahmin elsewhere whose teaching is as true, as real, as accurate as that of the Buddha?’

verses.pali: So evaṁ pajānāti:
verses.english: They understand:

verses.pali: ‘natthi kho ito bahiddhā añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo evaṁ bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ tathaṁ dhammaṁ deseti yathā bhagavā’ti.
verses.english: ‘There is no other ascetic or brahmin elsewhere whose teaching is as true, as real, as accurate as that of the Buddha.’

verses.pali: Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: This too is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee can understand that they are a trainee.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu pañcindriyāni pajānāti—
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant who is a trainee understands the five faculties:

verses.pali: saddhindriyaṁ, vīriyindriyaṁ, satindriyaṁ, samādhindriyaṁ, paññindriyaṁ.
verses.english: faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

verses.pali: Yaṅgatikāni yaṁparamāni yaṁphalāni yaṁpariyosānāni. Na heva kho kāyena phusitvā viharati;
verses.english: And although they don’t have direct meditative experience of their destination, apex, fruit, and culmination,

verses.pali: paññāya ca ativijjha passati.
verses.english: they do see them with penetrating wisdom.

verses.pali: Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: This too is a way that a mendicant who is a trainee can understand that they are a trainee.

verses.pali: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajānāti?
verses.english: And what is the way that a mendicant who is an adept can understand that they are an adept?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, asekho bhikkhu pañcindriyāni pajānāti—
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant who is an adept understands the five faculties:

verses.pali: saddhindriyaṁ, vīriyindriyaṁ, satindriyaṁ, samādhindriyaṁ, paññindriyaṁ.
verses.english: faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

verses.pali: Yaṅgatikāni yaṁparamāni yaṁphalāni yaṁpariyosānāni. Kāyena ca phusitvā viharati;
verses.english: They have direct meditative experience of their destination, apex, fruit, and culmination,

verses.pali: paññāya ca ativijjha passati.
verses.english: and they see them with penetrating wisdom.

verses.pali: Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: This is a way that a mendicant who is an adept can understand that they are an adept.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, asekho bhikkhu cha indriyāni pajānāti.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant who is an adept understands the six faculties:

verses.pali: ‘Cakkhundriyaṁ, sotindriyaṁ, ghānindriyaṁ, jivhindriyaṁ, kāyindriyaṁ, manindriyaṁ—
verses.english: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

verses.pali: imāni kho cha indriyāni sabbena sabbaṁ sabbathā sabbaṁ aparisesaṁ nirujjhissanti, aññāni ca cha indriyāni na kuhiñci kismiñci uppajjissantī’ti pajānāti.
verses.english: They understand: ‘These six faculties will totally and utterly cease without remainder. And no other six faculties will arise anywhere anyhow.’

verses.pali: Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṁ pariyāyaṁ āgamma asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṁ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajānātī”ti.
verses.english: This too is a way that a mendicant who is an adept can understand that they are an adept.”

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ.
